wave: CORRECTNESS / ARCHITECTURAL INTEGRITY -- duplicate, untested persistence-spelling classification logic
wave_title: adapter::semantic::rust::persistence's Expr::Call and Expr::MethodCall walker arms each carried their own independent copy of the same five-spelling (commit/flush/sync/sync_all/sync_data/checkpoint/snapshot) -> PersistenceKind match. The Expr::Call copy (used for a free/path-form call like `Store::commit(store)`) was not exercised by any existing test in PERSISTENCE_CORPUS, which uses only method-form calls -- so a future edit adding or changing a spelling in only one copy would have silently diverged with no test to catch it.

Noticed the Expr::MethodCall arm's inline match block was byte-for-byte the same five arms as the separately-named `persistence_candidate_kind` function used by the Expr::Call arm just above it, then confirmed via grep that no existing PERSISTENCE_CORPUS fixture used a free/path-form call, so the Expr::Call copy was live code with zero test coverage.

priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity (priority 1 in the fixed self-selection order) -- this repository has already fixed the identical defect class once this generation cycle for a different pair of walkers: R4.12's CALL/DATA_FLOW convergence fix (`call_argument_place_ref_converges_on_the_data_flow_uses_own_record_id`) factored a shared recognizer specifically 'to guarantee the two walkers cannot silently drift apart.' Leaving persistence.rs with the same duplicated-classification shape it had already been shown to be a real risk pattern in this codebase is exactly the kind of internal inconsistency this session's own engineering-quality standard flags.

design_decisions.question: Unify the two match blocks by having Expr::MethodCall call through `persistence_candidate_kind` (which takes a `&syn::Expr` and does its own spelling extraction), or extract a smaller shared `&str -> Option<PersistenceKind>` function?
design_decisions.decision: Extract `persistence_kind_for_spelling(name: &str) -> Option<PersistenceKind>`, the minimal shared surface. `persistence_candidate_kind` (Expr::Call) still does its own path-spelling extraction (via `call_callee_spelling` + last `::`-segment) since a free call's callee is a path expression, not a bare identifier; `Expr::MethodCall` already has the plain method name as a `syn::Ident` with no path to split, so forcing it through `call_callee_spelling`'s `Expr`-shaped API would be indirection with no benefit. Both now delegate the actual classification decision to the one shared function, which is the part that actually needed to never drift.

Combined with the 7 pre-existing PERSISTENCE tests (all still passing, all method-form), this is now the first test in the corpus to exercise `persistence_candidate_kind`'s Expr::Call branch at all.
